articleTitle: Application of guard traces with vias in the RF PCB layout
abstract: In this paper we discuss the effect of the guard traces with vias on the function of the parallel double microstrip lines in the PCB layout. The structure of the parallel double microstrip line is treated as a symmetrical network with 4 ports, simulation on the S parameters is processed; from the S parameters we can analyze the effect of the guard trace, then get the conclusion that the guard trace with vias is helpful to decrease the coupling strength between the double micro-strip lines.

articleTitle: A circuit approach to simulate discharge current injected in contact with an ESD-gun
abstract: An equivalent circuit modeling was proposed for simulating the discharge current injected in contact with an ESD-gun, which is being prescribed in the IEC 61000-4-2. Based on the structure and dimension of the ESD-gun, all the circuit parameters were determined from both calculation and measurement. The equivalent circuit derived here was validated by comparing the calculated waveform of the discharge current with the measured result.

articleTitle: The study and analysis of the conducted EMI suppression on power MOSFET using passive snubber circuits
abstract: This paper presents the study and analysis of RCD, RLD, and RCD-RLD passive snubber circuits affect on the power losses and suppression of the conducted EMI emission on the power MOSFET. The paper describes the snubber effects on dv/dt during the turn-off period, di/dt during the turn-on period, overvoltage, spike voltage, power loss and the conducted EMI emission. A 100 watt-50 kHz buck converter is used in the simulation and experiment. The measured and simulated results of conducted EMI emission are compared to verify the effectiveness of each snubber circuit.

articleTitle: High frequency model of common mode inductor for EMI analysis based on measurements
abstract: The high frequency characteristics of common mode (CM) inductors will affect their performance of conducted EMI suppression. This paper proposes a general procedure to construct a high frequency model of common mode inductors based on measurements in the frequency range from 9 kHz to 30 MHz. As an example, a lumped parameter high frequency model is given, in which CM inductance, leakage inductance, parasitic capacitance in winding and between windings, and ferrite resistance, etc, are described and determined based on measurements. Simulation demonstrates the model.

articleTitle: Application of segmentation method to analysis of power/ground plane resonance in multilayer PCBs
abstract: The fast algorithm developed for calculating the resonant characteristics of the power/ground planes in multilayer PCBs, is extended to the case of that the pattern of the power/ground planes consists of several "segments" of rectangles, using the so-called segmentation method. Good agreements between the calculated and measured results have demonstrated the usefulness and accuracy of our fast algorithm and the segmentation method.

articleTitle: Development of generator for voltage dips, short interruptions and voltage variations immunity test
abstract: This paper deals with the development of the generator for immunity test of voltage dips, short interruption and voltage variations, which occur widely in low-voltage mains and interfere with the electrical and electronic systems or equipment connected to the mains. The output voltage waveforms of the immunity test generator are full compliance with the GB/T 17626.11 and IEC 61000-4-11 standards. Experiments and preliminary tests toward typical DC regulated power supply have been done to testify the equipment's efficiency and feasibility. The resulting waveforms show that the generator can work very well.

articleTitle: A strategy for parallel implementation of the FDTD algorithm
abstract: This paper introduced a strategy for parallel implementation of the FDTD algorithm using a COW (cluster of workstations) parallel computing system. Some computing examples were given to prove the feasibility, correctness and high efficiency of this method. This method provides a solve-scheme for the EM computation of electrically large-sized complex objects and can be used in EMC analysis.

articleTitle: A high frequency transfer function model of potential transformer in GIS
abstract: For an accurate simulation of the voltage stress in secondary circuits caused by very fast transients (VFT) in gas insulated substation (GIS), a sophisticated modelling of the inductive potential and current transformers (PT/CT) is of vital importance. In this paper, we present a high frequency transfer function model of the potential transformer in GIS. The model's set up is based on the frequency response from 1 MHz to 60 MHz which was obtained by testing. We use rational function consisting of real poles as well as complex conjugate poles and zeros to approximate the frequency response. A new fitting method based on vector fitting to fit the frequency response only based on the magnitude frequency characteristics of the PT is proposed.

articleTitle: HVDC advanced analysis methods for grounding design and DC interference mitigation techniques
abstract: This paper presents advances made in HVDC grounding design techniques and the DC interference effects generated by HVDC ground electrodes on neighboring metallic utilities, with a particular emphasis on buried pipelines (oil, gas, water). The influence of soil structure on the performance of ground electrodes and on interference levels is demonstrated. A realistic case is modeled in detail to illustrate the accuracy, flexibility, and capabilities of these methods.

articleTitle: Modelling of magnetic hysteresis using Cauchy distribution
abstract: In this paper the Preisach model is used to simulate magnetic hysteresis. A Gaussian distribution is frequently applied as the distribution function of the model. The idea of using a Cauchy distribution to produce hysteresis loops is presented. The influence of each distribution parameter is shown. The calculated results are compared with the technical data of a sample. This study indicates that a Cauchy distribution can be applied favourably to simulate hysteresis loops.

articleTitle: EMI detection by means of wavelet
abstract: This paper proposes a new EMI detection approach. The approach uses a wavelet to analyze various waveforms (generated by CAD or measured by digital oscilloscope) in a particular circuit, identify specialized EMI spectrum distribution in the circuit layout in order to assist removing EMI quickly. An EMI detection application for a DC-DC converter is also offered.

articleTitle: A new kind of lightning channel-base current function
abstract: In allusion to the disadvantages of double exponential function and Heidler function which are widely used to describe lightning channel-base current, a new kind of lightning channel-base current model is presented. The comparison among the three kinds of function shows that the new function is predominant over the other two. It is highly efficient in calculating lightning electromagnetic pulse fields (LEMP).

articleTitle: Active shielding design for a MV/LV distribution transformer substation
abstract: The shielding of the low frequency magnetic field is obtained by using a system of fed active coils that produce a magnetic field opposite to the incident one reducing the total magnetic field. In this paper the design of a real active shield system is proposed to mitigate the magnetic field in the MV/LV distribution transformer substation located at the Engineering Building of the University of L'Aquila. The design of the active shield system is developed starting from the experimental data obtained by the measurement of the magnetic field inside the MV/LV substation.

articleTitle: Wide-band electromagnetic wave absorber of rubber-ferrite
abstract: Two different compositions with Ba(Ti/sub 0.5/Co/sub 0.5/)/sub 2.1/Fe/sub 9.9/ O/sub 19/ and Ba(Ti/sub 0.5/Co/sub 0.5/)/sub 3.2/Fe/sub 8.8/O/sub 19/ of barium ferrite with a magnetoplumbite structure (M-type) had been obtained by conventional ceramic technology. The complex permeability and permittivity of the materials were measured in the 2-18 GHz band. Ba M-type ferrite materials mixed with polyvinyl chloride, plasticizer and frit are pressed to form flakes (180 mm/spl times/180 mm/spl times/2 mm) of rubber-ferrite. The absorption properties of the single layer rubber-ferrite absorber are measured by an Agilent 8722ES network analyzer (2-18 GHz). Compared with the theoretical calculation, it was found that preferable properties of microwave absorption were obtained by using a bank of two ferrite materials singly over a narrow frequency region. Almost all of the samples in the multi-layer rubber-ferrite absorber exhibited a minimum reflection loss less than -10 dB with a thickness (d/sub m/) 22 mm.

articleTitle: Application of the electromagnetic field method to study a communication satellite site damaged by lightning
abstract: This paper presents a case study of a satellite communications site at which equipment was damaged during a lightning storm. The transient ground potential rise (GPR) and stress voltages on the damaged equipment (HPA) during a lightning storm are obtained using the electromagnetic field theory method. The stress voltage on the HPA is reduced by 75% (from 25 kV to 6 kV) when the isolated signal ground wire is electrically bonded to a nearby equipment ground. An extended grounding system has little influence on the stress voltages at the beginning of the transient period; however, it reduces the stress voltages significantly (by about 50%) after the first 3 /spl mu/s.

articleTitle: Heatsink grounding effect on radiated emission of electronic device
abstract: Heatsink is an indispensable component in electronic device. However, containing emissions from heatsink is rapidly becoming a necessity caused by higher power levels and faster clocking of digital circuits, it affects the sensitive circuit. Some grounding schemes of heatsink are presented and calculated applying the FDTD method. It is shown that different grounding point affect the electromagnetic characteristic of a heatsink differently,. and more grounding points do not mean the improvement of electromagnetic characteristic. Considering four grounding points, four edge centered ground points is selected for a small electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: X-band slotted antenna: practical part
abstract: Slot array antennas are used for marine navigation, radars, and telemetry systems and for reception of microwave television signals in the multipoint distribution service (MDS) at 2.145 GHz. The prime purpose of this paper is to present the practical part of an X-band slotted array antenna. The design is made for frequency of 10 GHz. The bandwidth of the array is narrow while its gain is relatively high. The feeding technique is designed to maintain constant phase for all elements of the array. Manufacturing simplicity is optimized with the required features and characteristics of the antenna. Such an array is a linear one. The antenna consists of seventeen juxtaposed waveguides for operation in the X-band. The antenna structure is designed such that corner reflections are avoided. Precise location and optimum dimensions of slots are described. Also feeding of the array is included. Practical dimensions of the array are calculated. The radiation pattern in both E and H planes and voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) are accurately measured. There is good agreement between the measured and the calculated results.

articleTitle: Analysis of enclosure with an aperture using FDTD method
abstract: A shielding enclosure with an aperture is modeled and simulated by using the FDTD method. The case of a plane wave source is discussed, and the transmitted field through an aperture and the shielding effectiveness inside the enclosure are calculated. Some results are obtained. The results of the FDTD and ETL methods are compared.

articleTitle: A new FDTD algorithm - ADI/R-FDTD
abstract: Making use of the two modified finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, that is, ADI-FDTD and R-FDTD, we propose a new time domain method in this paper. The method is established from Maxwell curl and divergence equations. It inherits the advantages of both former methods, i.e., not only eliminating the restraint of the Courant-Friedrich-Levy (C-F-L) condition, with an efficient saving of CPU time, but also leading to a direct memory reduction of 33% in the storage of the field components. The formulation is presented and some results of numerical examples are compared to FDTD, ADI-FDTD and R-FDTD. Good agreement is observed.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of microwave ovens
abstract: This paper describes the measurements of the radiation from microwave ovens. The measurements at the frequency of 2.45 GHz are performed under different test conditions, and the radiations of different types of microwave ovens are measured from 30 MHz to 1000 MHz. The test results are presented to compare the radiations emitted from different types of microwave ovens. Also the radiation characteristics of a microwave oven are concluded in this paper.

articleTitle: Determination of rail conductor characteristics for electromagnetic interference studies
abstract: This paper describes the approach used to establish a dynamic rail conductor characteristics database for the accurate simulation of complex realistic right-of-way electromagnetic interference problems. The equivalent model of the rail, interpolation methods and the rail conductor database are presented in detail. A typical example involving electromagnetic interference between high voltage power transmission lines and a railway is used to illustrate the use of the dynamic rail conductor database.

articleTitle: On compromising emanations from computer VDU and its interception
abstract: VDU is the main source of electromagnetic emanations of computer system. The acceleration field and radiated field of the equivalent electric dipole of the electron beam in CRT are both analyzed as well as that of deflection coils. They an cause risk to information security of VDU. Method to reconstruct video information by intercepting emanations form VDU is discussed in this paper and an intercepting system is presented, with which trusty experimental results are acquired.

articleTitle: The use of an optically modulated scatterer to measure the performance of microwave electromagnetic wave absorber
abstract: The optically modulated scatterer (OMS) can be used to measure the standing wave distribution of microwave electromagnetic fields with minimum intrusiveness. This paper reports the measurement by OMS of a new commercially developed pyramidal ferrite absorber between 2 GHz and 18 GHz. The results are analysed and compared with those by other RF and microwave measurement methods.

articleTitle: Prediction of switching transient electromagnetic fields in gas-insulated substations
abstract: Due to the opening or closing operation of circuit breakers and disconnected switches in gas-insulated substations (GIS), a very strong transient wave process can be generated along the three-phase transmission system and transient electromagnetic field can be radiated from the junction between the GIS enclosure and the high-voltage cables. Based on a kind of hybrid method, the software TEMFGIS is provided to predict the radiated field in time domain. Its validity is verified by the measurement results.

articleTitle: Crosstalk prediction in twisted bundles by a neural approach
abstract: A neural network based procedure is proposed for the crosstalk prediction in twisted bundles. The nonuniform bundle is approximated as a cascade of uniform sections and the neural network is suitably trained with few cross section configurations to learn the behavior of the per unit length parameters. The procedure allows a fast and accurate prediction tool.

articleTitle: A time-domain microwave oven noise model for evaluation of interfered communication system performance
abstract: For analyzing the interference in a radio communication system caused by a microwave oven, a time-domain noise model is newly developed taking into account the noise generation mechanism. It is a very simple model made of an FM/AM modulator. Comparison between an actual noise and the proposed model in the waveforms and spectra clearly demonstrates the usefulness of the proposed one.

articleTitle: EMC problem in a train control system based on wireless communications
abstract: A wireless locomotive signal system (WLSS) is the kernel of a new train control system. Applying the wireless communication system as a flat roof of information transmission, the system has achieved bipolar transmission between the vehicle and the console of the railway station. Different from the traditional locomotive signal system that uses track circuits as information transmitting channels, a WLSS has the advantages that the functions of communications and control are integrated and the capacity of information transmitting is large. The author attended to the research work of the system. Based on the working principles of the system, this paper mainly discusses the EMC problems in the system and puts forward the solutions.

articleTitle: Impulse transient characteristic of grounding grids
abstract: The lightning transient characteristics of a substation grounding grid are analyzed in detail, especially considering the dynamic and nonlinear effects of soil ionization around grounding conductors and the inductance between grounding conductors. The analysis results are calculated by a loss transmission-line model with distributed time-variable parameter. The influences of grid structure, feed point location, and shape of the lightning impulse current on the transient characteristics of grounding grids are discussed.

articleTitle: Interaction of EMC, acoustics and thermal management in the reliable operation of a data center
abstract: To design a highly reliable data center, it requires careful consideration of many factors. In this paper, the importance of EMC, acoustics, and thermal management and the relationships between them are discussed. The basic design guidelines of each, and their important role within the data center space to achieve high availability especially from a thermal management viewpoint and its interaction with EMC are carefully reviewed.

articleTitle: Magnetic shielding by large metallic structure in modern buildings
abstract: In high-rise commercial buildings, the concept of raised floors and metal decking is often adopted for various purposes. The shielding performance of these metal structures is of interest. The paper presents an experimental investigation into the shielding properties of raised floors, metal decking and large flat sheets applied in buildings. It is recognized that the shielding performance depends on various parameters, such as shielding material, source orientation, shield thickness, and distance from the shield. These factors should be carefully looked at when magnetic shielding is considered to mitigate background magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Automatic test system of the antenna characteristic
abstract: The antenna is a component used to transmit or receive electric waves in a wireless communicating system. At the transmitting terminal its primary function is to change electrical current of high frequency transmitted by transmitter or, transmission line into a wireless wave and transmit it into space; at the receiving terminal it changes the energy of the wireless wave into electrical current. Then, we can regard antenna as transforming equipment between conducting waves and radiate waves. The antenna has an important influence on the normal working of wireless communication, broadcasting, orientation and telemetry system. The antenna has influence on EMC just as important as that which it has on communication. In EMC emission measurements, EMI testing and EMS testing included; the antenna acts as the receiving component and the transmitting component separately. The antenna is the important equipment that receives the energy of radiation and it also is the important equipment that sends electromagnetic signals to the object that being tested. Thus, if there is no antenna, we cannot go on with our EMC testing. Any antenna has some characteristic parameters, which can be used to estimate this antenna's performance. These characteristic parameters include antenna impedance, directional property, antenna gain, posture, and the polarization characteristic, which determine that an antenna is fine and the area that it can be used in. So, these characteristic parameters have a great influence on the measuring result and the area it is used in. As every worker of EMC testing knows, it is very difficult to measure an antenna's characteristic parameters, some of which are not even measured by the current method. Some people try to measure them, but it takes much time and labor testing with conventional testing methods (i.e. testing by hand). What's more, it is easy to introduce testing errors. With the development of computers and the emergence of advanced testing equipment, it is necessary and possible to design a convenient automatic testing system for the antenna performance.

articleTitle: Experimental study of ESD effect on metallic enclosure
abstract: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) can cause serious problems in digital electronic devices. Indirect coupling through apertures on the metallic enclosure to the internal circuitries can also affect the performance of the devices. In this paper, we investigate experimentally the effect of the coupling field through apertures on the metallic enclosure.

articleTitle: Capacitive discharge of metallic structures close to high voltage power lines
abstract: A study of capacitive discharge of metallic structures that are close to high voltage power lines has been carried out. An equivalent circuit for modeling the transient capacitive discharge phenomenon is presented and analytical expressions for this transient behavior have been derived. Numerical results have been obtained and compared with published results for initial value of the transient potential and potential peaks after the steady-state conditions have been established. The agreement is excellent. The equivalent circuit model and analytical expressions for the transient behavior of the capacitive discharge process presented in this paper can be easily applied to many practical situations.

articleTitle: Simulation of microwave oven interference on digital radio communication systems
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of microwave oven (MWO) interference that severely degrades the performance of digital radio communication systems. At first, we study the statistical characteristics of MWO interference by analyzing the measurements. Then we propose an improved simulation method by which interference data can be acquired with the statistical characteristics similar to MWO interference. Finally, our simulation results are applied to discuss the receiving techniques for improving the performance of DS/CDMA systems under MWO interference environment.

articleTitle: EMP energy transfer function on EED
abstract: The hazards of electromagnetic radiation to ordnance (HERO) program has extensively tested the detonating device, called electro-explosive device (EED), which heats up and initiates detonation via current flow. EED accidents can occur due to the action of an electromagnetic pulse (EMP). Any kind of system can be considered as an antenna to receive EMP energy and this energy may couple to the EED. The EED and its related problems are introduced and heat flow equations are studied. The amount and type of current induced in wires to an EED depends on the type of receiving antenna. Three basic types of antenna are discussed, loop antenna, dipole antenna and top-loaded antenna.

articleTitle: A new version of DCSK data transmission scheme
abstract: In this paper a new version of DCSK scheme is proposed, which can double the data rate without increasing any complexity of the chaotic communication system. Then the advantages and disadvantages of this scheme are discussed.

articleTitle: A comprehensive analysis method of conducted EMI of an off-line converter
abstract: In this paper, the conducted EMI characteristic of an off-line converter is analyzed in detail. Considering the high frequency switches as main EMI sources, a group of simple equations can be deduced, which describe the typical relationship among EMI emissions, the noise sources and the coupling paths. Based on the equations, a novel measurement is proposed to characterize the conducted EMI coupling paths. According to the equations and the characteristics of coupling paths, the different roles of dv/dt and di/dt in high frequency switches on conducted EMI emissions can be analyzed concretely. An equivalent CM conducted EMI model is synthesized according to the curves of coupling paths and the main stray parameters of the converter. This model avoids complicated stray parameters extraction process and is useful for the design of EMI filer.

articleTitle: Introduction to reverberation chamber test method and a two-stirrer mini-reverberation chamber
abstract: As a time-efficient and cost-effective EMC test facility candidate, the reverberation chamber has attracted much attention from academia and industries. The objective of the paper is to introduce its general background, standardisation status and practical applications, highlighting some of merit and non-merit associated with the reverberation chamber test method. A mini-reverberation chamber made of aluminium with two orthogonal and mechanical stirrers is also presented.

articleTitle: Different mode conducted EMI of three-phase SCR rectifier: prediction and reduction
abstract: This paper analyzes the EMI that is generated from a three-phase SCR rectifier and the effect of some common reduction measures. According to the switching function, the noise equivalent circuit is obtained. Based on these equivalent circuits, the noise spectrum calculation can be performed in the frequency-domain. The experiment results show the validity of the calculation. Since the calculation is in the frequency-domain, it does not need many parasitic parameters and the calculation time can be greatly decreased compared with time-domain simulation.

articleTitle: FDTD modeling of skin effect
abstract: The data rates and clock speeds of current high-speed signals are increasing rapidly, consequently, not only the lossy nature of FR-4 but also the lossy nature of good conductors, such as copper, need to be taken into account in high-speed signal designs. In order to predict the loss caused by both dielectric loss and skin effect loss, a suitable simulation tool is needed. A surface impedance boundary condition (SIBC) algorithm was implemented in FDTD modeling herein to accommodate the skin effect loss due to finite conductivity of good conductors. Good agreement between the FDTD result and the measurements as well as the SPICE result was obtained for a 14 mils wide strip line.

articleTitle: Analysis of slot-eavesdrop of coaxial cable with FDTD method
abstract: In this paper, the perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbing boundary condition is applied to a general finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) in a 3D cylindrical coordinates system. We deduce the difference formulation both in free space and the PML field, and the axial singularities are removed by using Ampere's law. With this method, the characteristics of a coaxial cable slot-eavesdrop are discussed. In the simulation, the singularities near the metal edge are removed using the Fourier-Bessel expansion. It shows that research of electromagnetic eavesdropping in coaxial cable interfaces in the electromagnetic compatibility field is needed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the effectiveness of ferrite core for improving EFT immunity
abstract: This paper analysis the effectiveness of ferrite core for improving electrical fast transient (EFT) immunity of electronic apparatus and equipment. In this study, we examine the impedances of two ferrite cores made from different materials. Where possible, the measured results for EFT suppression effectiveness of ferrite cores with different impedance characteristic are also included.

articleTitle: Keep out of the Western protection standards
abstract: The philosophy of Western standards is based upon specific absorption rate (SAR) estimations. Then, on the basis of an absorption model analysis, the protection levels are calculated. The accuracy of the procedure is on the level of one order of magnitude. On the other hand the levels and their frequency dependencies and frequency ranges are given with an accuracy of four significant figures. It is illogical as the result must not be given with an accuracy exceeding that of the introductory data. An example a proposed solution is presented.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of shielded high frequency coaxial transformer for switching power supplies
abstract: The paper presents the configuration of a high frequency coaxial transformer with a Faraday shield and discusses the shielding effect and insertion loss at a high frequency range for the switch mode power supplies. The numerical computation and visualization results demonstrate the magnetic flux and eddy current distribution in the windings and Faraday shield. The shielding effectiveness of a Faraday shield in a high frequency coaxial transformer is also investigated by using a high frequency equivalent circuit model and Pspice simulation. The experimental results demonstrate the voltage ratio, coupling coefficient and load characteristic of the high frequency coaxial transformer with Faraday shield in the range up to 2 MHz.

articleTitle: Calculation of transient electric field inside the building struck by lightning
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient method for calculating transient electric field inside the building struck by lightning. The analytical description of transient electric field is given by the vector potential on the basis of Maxwell equations. The vector potential is further expressed by the lightning current traveling along an arbitrary branch of building's lightning protection system. With a reasonable simplification made in consideration of the field components, an approximate formula is derived for evaluating transient electric field in terms of the lightning current. The numerical solution is then obtained by performing a discretization treatment to the approximate formula. Finally, an electric field distribution is illustrated for a tall building to confirm the capability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Shielding performance of a metallic enclosure with slots - numerical modelling and measurements
abstract: The shielding performance of a rectangular metallic enclosure with two slots is analysed using a fullwave electromagnetic simulation software based on the method of moments. Measurements are conducted in a 3m semi-anechoic chamber to validate the results. A good agreement between the results gives confidence in the simulation. Thus. simulation tools can be used to predict and optimise the shielding performance of metallic enclosures.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness of multilayered shields for magnetic field nonsinusoidal sources
abstract: The magnetic field generated by a nonsinusoidal periodic source is shielded by a planar infinite multilayered shield composed of high permeability and high conductivity materials. By means of a transform analytical approach, the shielding effectiveness is calculated.

articleTitle: Lightning electromagnetic radiation field spectra in the interval from 25 to 100 MHz
abstract: By means of a fast Fourier transform (FFT), average energy spectra in the interval from 25 to 100 MHz are presented for most of the components that produce large radiation field pulses from lightning: first and subsequent return strokes; stepped and dart leaders; preliminary breakdown and intracloud K changes.

articleTitle: Sheath currents and magnetic fields of single-pole encapsulated switchgear installations
abstract: The production of magnetic fields from single pole encapsulated switchgear installations is significantly determined by the propagation of sheath currents on the encapsulation. This paper outlines investigations concerning the creation of sheath currents, concerning their distribution on the encapsulation as well as their influence on the resulting magnetic fields caused by the switchgear. Numerical simulations on the basis of the method of moments were performed which take into account the induction of sheath currents and which were used to calculate magnetic field distributions in the vicinity of single-pole encapsulated switchgear. The numerical data were compared with results obtained by measurements at real switchgear installations.

articleTitle: Equivalent simplified parallel multi-conductors model of shielded control cable in substation
abstract: The electromagnetic coupling between the control cable with metal shielding sheath and metal conductor of grounding grids in the substation of a power system threatens the safe operation of an electronic system connected with the control cable. In order to simplifying the electromagnetic coupling analysis of this system, the core-sheath model of a control cable is replaced by a parallel multi-conductor model with theoretical analysis and numerical computation in this paper. From analysis of the resistance and the self-inductance of the sheath, the mutual inductance and the capacitance between the core and the sheath in both models, four nonlinear equations to solve the four unknown parameters in the parallel multi-conductors model are established. A program has also been coded to solve the equations. The results of the parallel multi-conductors model are compared with the analyzed ones of the actual control cable by the PSCAD software package. They have good agreement with each other.

articleTitle: Power frequency magnetic fields around busbar trunking risers
abstract: Busbar systems are often employed as a riser for power distribution in large buildings. The magnetic fields around typical busbar trunking systems are evaluated in this paper via numerical and experimental investigation. Galvanized iron enclosure of the busbar trunking system is approximately modeled as a linear enclosure with a constant equivalent relative permeability. The modeling effectiveness is validated. It is found that the equivalent relative permeability is almost linearly proportional the magnitude of the carried current. Harmonic frequency magnetic fields are also discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of the electromagnetic constants of concrete materials by time-domain reflectometry
abstract: A dielectric constant and electrical conductivity measurement system based on time-domain reflectometry (TDR) probes that can be embedded into concrete structures have been designed. The calibration data in distilled water has shown that the measuring system can measure the dielectric constant and conductivity accurately. By using the embedded probes in concrete structures, changes of the electromagnetic properties through the curing stage of Portland concrete specimens are measured and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Iterative method of maximum likelihood for estimation of non-Gaussian probability density of signals and interferences
abstract: This work offered the resulting probability density of set of signal (interference) parameters to describe through a mixture of private probability densities. For definition of unknown parameters of private probability densities it is offered to use iterative method of maximum likelihood. This method is new; it is essential in relation to classical method of maximum likelihood. In the report the proofs of optimality of method and it reducibility in the classical method are outlined. The considered iterative procedure is applied for the identification of classes of one-dimensional stochastic signals.

articleTitle: The full wave analysis of fractal antennas
abstract: The full wave method (FDTD) was used to analyse some fractal antennas. The computational results are in good agreement with the experiments for the Hilbert curve fractal antenna. The results show that fractal geometries can be implemented to miniaturize the antenna size compared to the normal antenna. Also the self-similar nature in the Sierpinski fractal geometry can be utilized for operating a fractal antenna at various frequencies. Furthermore, the far field patterns of the fractal antennas remain almost the same at their resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Investigation on the status quo of EMC in Chinese power system
abstract: The status quo of electromagnetic compatibility in the Chinese power system was investigated. The types, the characteristics of electromagnetic interference (EMI) within the power system were analyzed, and the examples about typical accidents resulting from EMI were given, which may call attention to EMC in the power system.

articleTitle: Loss transmission-line model of grounding electrodes considering soil ionization of lightning impulse
abstract: A loss transmission-line model with distributed time-variable parameter for the calculation of transient characteristic of a grounding system under lightning to consider the dynamic and nonlinear effect of soil ionization around the ground electrode is proposed. The influences of the length of grounding electrodes and location of feed point on the transient characteristic of ground electrodes are analyzed. Grounding electrodes have impulse effective length under impulse current. The model has been validated by comparing the numerical results with experimental tests.

articleTitle: Understanding shielding performance of screened rooms
abstract: The paper discusses the principles and issues for the shielding of a screened room. It does not go into the details of general shielding design, but specifically looks at screened rooms and their parameters, including performance, testing and specifications. The reason for producing this document is that the author has seen many different manufacturers' designs and claims (realistic or otherwise) which severely confuse the potential end-user. The aim is to clarify these issues and produce a reference document by which the potential user of a screened room is able to make informed judgements on what is required, what is feasible and where potential problems may lie, hopefully getting the best product/price performance ratio.

articleTitle: Effects of propagation on the return stroke radiation fields
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the effects of the height of channel, the return stroke speed and the permittivity of ground on the return stroke radiation fields based on TL, MTLE, TCS and BG model. We assume a common current wave shape at the channel base and then calculate the electromagnetic field under different conditions. Some useful conclusions have been made in the paper.

articleTitle: The study of crosstalk in high-speed circuit design
abstract: In high-speed circuit design, crosstalk between traces is a very serious problem. They can couple unwanted signals to each other. When there is no slot, the return path is just under the trace and the current is in opposite direction. The interference current is small because the cancel effect of the image current. But when there is slot on the reference plane, the return current have to find another path around the slots and this effect will create obvious potential for crosstalk between the signal returns and in some circumstances the crosstalk could be very strong. In this paper, we study crosstalk with FDTD method especially for the slotted ground case. The result of this paper is very useful to the high-speed circuit design. We can use these results in the practical high-speed circuit design.

articleTitle: A circuit model of buried metallic pipelines for the evaluation of shielding effectiveness to nearby communication lines
abstract: A universal model is presented to evaluate the shielding effectiveness of underground metallic pipeline network near power lines to communication lines, which takes both inductive and resistive coupling between power lines and pipelines into account. The model is based on transmission line theory. Each pipeline is treated as an active two-port network and is equivalent to a PI-type circuit with lumped current sources. A simultaneous equation group, whose unknown quantities are nodal voltages of the pipeline network, is constructed to solve the current distribution. The shielding effectiveness of the underground metallic pipeline network to the communication lines can be obtained. The model is time-saving because the parameter of the PI-type model can be calculated analytically, while the size of memory required is very small. The model is of significance to the design and the rights-of-way selection of power lines and communication lines.

articleTitle: Modeling electromagnetic interference to computer and information equipment arise from coaxial cable with aperture
abstract: Electromagnetic wave, such as EMP, HPM and EML, may cause harmful effects or electromagnetic emission security attacks (EMES attacks) on computer and information equipment through connecting cables, especially when the cable has connector or apertures on the shield of the cable. EM wave may penetrate into the cable and propagate into computers and equipment connecting the cable with apertures. Because cables or transmission lines form a very large collector of the externally generated electromagnetic energy, the interference mechanics of the coupling through aperture on the cable sheath is different from the case of coupling through an aperture on the infinitive large conduction plane. The modeling work is made, in which both EM penetration and propagation effects of the EM wave are considered. The transmission effects of the induced current in the cable are also considered.

articleTitle: ADC design techniques in DRFM system based on EMC
abstract: Based on EMC, in DRFM system, design techniques of high speed and high accuracy ADCs with interference-free ability and low noise are described in this paper. After EMI model has been found, ideal performances can be achieved by analyzing interference factors, restraining interference sources and cutting off interference paths with corresponding steps. Important parameters, such as IBW, output SNR, frequency reproduction precision and MTBF, etc., can meet the needs of engineering design.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparison on image feature detectors
abstract: A number of image feature detectors and their characteristics are analyzed. The key issues of image feature detection are discussed extensively and comprehensively. Gradient-based feature detectors, their properties, and faults are discussed and phase-based techniques and their problems are also explained. Based on the survey, some open issues, which need to be researched further, are presented, and the future research trends are also discussed.

articleTitle: FDTD-simulation of the electrical environment for vehicles by using CAD-data
abstract: A method to make a CAD-model of a vehicle suitable for electromagnetic (EM) simulations is presented. Three different EMC problems have been studied by using the derived CAD-models in a finite difference time domain (FDTD) program. First, the coupling between antennas mounted on the vehicle. Second, the locations of "hot spots", i.e. places with high field strength inside the vehicle. Finally, the E-field probed in a circle around the vehicle. The agreement between simulations and measurements performed in a semi-anechoic chamber was found to be satisfactorily.

articleTitle: Speedy calculation of frequency-dependent impedances of underground power cables
abstract: This paper describes a speedy method for calculation of frequency-dependent series impedances of the underground power cable in a tunnel. These impedances are needed for the analysis of electromagnetic transients and EMC in power systems. A technique based on the fictitious medium concept is used to calculate the magnetic vector potential exactly at several single frequencies in the tunnel, which reduces the solution region inside the poorly conducting earth. The frequency characteristic of power cable is obtained by a very powerful extrapolating approach, i.e. Cauchy method. The extrapolating results are compared with those from the frequency point-by-point matching approach. The method is very time saving because only the low rank frequency derivative information of the power cable impedance is required.

articleTitle: The analysis and feature extraction of nonstationary random characteristics of radar jammer signal
abstract: Nonstationary random signals have been the hot topic in domestic and overseas research recently. Mostly various signals studied in EMC are random jammer and nonstationary signals. The paper discusses stability judgement and feature extraction, proceeds to time-frequency analysis based on the Wigner-Ville distribution, and presents a practical example of radar jammer signals. The study can be applied to suppress jammer signals in EMC and offer jammer signal sources for experimental research by means of stimulation and emulation.

articleTitle: An analysis on anti-interference performance of phase-inversion symmetric modulation and its application in the field of EMC
abstract: Phase-inversion symmetric modulation (PISM) is a new communication method proposed ten years ago which has extremely strong anti-interference capacity. Theoretically and practically, this method can be widely used in the field of EMC.

articleTitle: FM EMF sensors
abstract: The development of the photonic sensors for electromagnetic field measurements is presented. The first applications were limited to telemetry only. An advantage of photonic sensors is the preserved spectral and phase information. An improvement in the sensors' sensitivity is illustrated with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and internal FM modulation of a laser with heterodyne detection. A concept of the sensor with a Fabry-Perot filter as a wideband frequency discriminator is introduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of conducted EMI emission on a soft-switched boost converter using a single switch
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of a soft-switched boost converter using a single switch and low reactive components without the auxiliary active switches for achieving zero-voltage turn on and zero-current turn off. The paper describes the operating characteristics, and analyzes the overall performance compared with the conventional boost converter. A comparison of conducted electromagnetic interference emission of conventional and proposed circuits is also included. In addition, the experimental results are in good agreement with the theoretical ones.

articleTitle: LEMP coupling with medium voltage overhead lines and its effects on low voltage networks with power electronic devices
abstract: Using a novel combined algorithm based on an antenna theory model and the Electromagnetic Transients Program, we study how the induced overvoltage on overhead lines due to a nearby lightning stroke is propagated in a distribution network with power electronic devices. It is shown that the presence of surge protection devices can considerably reduce the induced overvoltage, provided that they are placed properly in the network.

articleTitle: Analysis design and application of sphere loaded monopole antenna
abstract: This paper analyzed and studied configurations of the rotationally symmetric monopole antenna by applying the extended moment method. Its terminal uses a sphere-loaded technique. The optimum cone angle is obtained and the curve of the lower cut-off frequency versus height is discussed. A sphere loaded antenna is designed and fabricated for impulse radar. Theoretical calculations and partial experimental results are compared and reasonable agreement is obtained. The research provides a theoretical basis for practical design.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics and scaling law of seismo-electric field
abstract: Electric field around a crack in rock is generated by the appearance and subsequent disappearance of charges on a newly created surface. This electric field occurs here and there along a fault plane. We record it as one of seismo-electromagnetic phenomena (SEP). In a simple case, the maximum of the field is proportional to the surface charge density and the total real contact area of a fault plane. A new scaling law between the maximum of the seismo-electric field and the earthquake magnitude is obtained based on the fractal distribution of fault asperities. It can support the VAN group's statistical scaling law.

articleTitle: Standardization activity in the field of EMC
abstract: This paper presents the standardization work which is performed in the framework of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) in the Technical Committee 77 and in CISPR. The introduction of the EMC Directive for products put on the European market is also discussed. The paper defines also basic, generic and product standards. As EMC concerns many products, TC77 has a horizontal function and to achieve it, IEC Guide 107 has been developed. The coordination work on EMC in all Technical Committees performed by the Advisory Committee on EMC (ACEC) is also discussed together with future trends in trade and their impact on the EMC aspect of manufacturing products.

articleTitle: Analysis of a broad wall waveguide slot coupler by FDTD method
abstract: An analysis of a broad wall slot coupler between two crossed rectangular waveguides using the FDTD method is presented in this paper. Two types of slot, a longitudinal/transverse slot and a centered-inclined slot, are analyzed. Coupling slot characteristics are obtained, including scattering parameters and the resonant length in different waveguide dimensions and frequencies. A type of coupler system with a short circuit port is also analyzed.

articleTitle: The analysis of a ridged conical horn with FEM
abstract: This paper discusses properties of a wideband conical horn antenna, of which the tapered portion has four ridges mounted symmetrically. Taking advantage of the FEM method, the authors succeed in calculating various cut-off wavelengths and electromagnetic fields at different cross sections of the ridged tapered circular waveguide. Based on the results, the VSWR of the tapered portion is evaluated correctly and the results show that the antenna can work well within the 2-18 GHz band (with VSWR lower than 2.0).

articleTitle: Study of generalized resonance in antenna system
abstract: This paper begins with a complete description of the complex Poynting theorem, followed by a rigorous study of the generalized resonance in an antenna system. We discuss the generalized resonance, which is the balance of the electromagnetic field energy stored in an antenna open system. The matrix expression of the generalized resonant factor is derived. Some realistic examples have shown that the generalized resonance may take on the frequency response of the strong peak value field in the near field region and super-directivity in the far field region of the antenna system.

articleTitle: A study of electromagnetic characteristics of Fe-Si-Al magnetic alloy
abstract: Fe-Si-Al magnetic alloy powders, consisting of Si 9.7wt%-Al 5.4wt%-bal Fe, were prepared by mechanical alloying. The appearance, phase composition, complex permeability /spl mu//spl dot/, complex permittivity /spl epsiv//spl dot/ of different milling time samples were measured respectively by SEM, X-ray diffraction and microwave vector network analysis in the 2-18 GHz band. Variations of the electromagnetic characteristics in the mechanical alloying process were analyzed. The aspect ratio of samples increased with the milling time, and the aspect ratio about 50-60 of the 300 h milling sample was observed by SEM. The X-ray diffraction peak of the 300 h milling sample was the most screechy, and the values of /spl mu/' and /spl mu/" were over 3.7 and 2.0 respectively. The frequency dependence of reflection loss of the 300 h milling samples with different thickness was measured by the Agilent 8722ES microwave vector network analyzer. Result showed that the electromagnetic characteristics of the materials can be controlled by the variation of the mechanical alloying process. These novel materials can be used in EMC systems.

articleTitle: Study on the magnetic shielding composite coating in low frequency
abstract: A new type of magnetic shielding coating in low frequency (f/spl les/20 kHz) was made. The fillers of the coating were compound. They were made of non-crystal magnetic powder, micron Ni powder and magnetic fibre. The agglomerant of the coating was acrylic resin. The coating was gained after surface treating, mixing, milling, grinding, filtrating techniques. The maximum magnetic shielding effectiveness of the coating is 14/spl sim/15 dB. The coating is low in cost, and convenient for application. The coating can reduce magnetic radiation pollution. We first found that the magnetic shielding in low frequency could be realized with the form of the coating.

articleTitle: Electric and electromagnetic shielding properties of highly conducting polyaniline films
abstract: The increasing use of commercial, military, and scientific electrical products and electronic devices has raised the problem of electromagnetic interference (EMI), also called electromagnetic environmental pollution, so there is an increased interest in EMI shielding. By use of mechanical mixing doping method, highly conducting polyaniline (PANI) films were prepared by the variation of dopant (camphor sulphonic acid) loading and solvent types in this paper. When dopant/emeradine base repeat unit molar ratio is 0.5/1, the conductivity of doped PANI is maximum. The conductivity results show that using m-cresol as solvent is better than N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NMP). Using such mechanical mixing doping method is better than other doping methods. It employs less solvent and less dopant. The maximum conductivity of the prepared films is up to 370 S/cm. Total shielding efficiency (SE/sub T/) of highly conducting polyaniline films was measured at 10 GHz of microwave frequency. Their dependence of SE/sub T/ on thickness of polyaniline films was studied. Shielding efficiencies (SE/sub T/) of PANI films were also measured in shielding room according to MIL-STD-285 standard in a different frequency. When the thickness of the film is 45 /spl mu/m, the measured SE/sub T/ is more than 40 dB. The SE/sub T/ result shows that the electromagnetic shielding property of highly conducting PANI film can meet the desire of commercial standard. Electromagnetic shielding efficiencies of different thickness films are calculated by far-field shielding theory. The practical measured SE/sub T/ values are compared with the calculated values. It is found that the measured SE/sub T/ values are very consistent with the theoretical calculated ones.

articleTitle: Shielding and energy transfer of transient electromagnetic fields
abstract: For the time-harmonic electromagnetic fields the shielding effectiveness of conducting and permeable materials is characterized by the relation of the field amplitudes or their quadratures arising at chosen locations in the absence of the electromagnetic shield to the ones arising in the presence of it. In theoretical treatises homogeneous electric or magnetic fields, plane fields of parallel conductors, homogeneous plane waves, or fields of elementary electromagnetic radiating sources are considered. This work presents a study of the transient field excited by a current loop i(t) of arbitrary time dependence and arbitrary contour in the presence of a plane, conducting, and permeable screen of finite thickness. The shielding effectiveness of the screen is characterized by the time dependence of the electromagnetic energy transfer into the shielded area caused by switched or pulsed sources.

articleTitle: A method to accelerate the calibration of RF-EMS test
abstract: This paper introduces a method to accelerate the calibration of RF-EMS test - "calculation approach method". The RF-EMS automatic test software generally uses "step by step approach method" to calibrate the test field. During the calibration, the "step by step approach method" needs several times of "setting the amplitude of output signal and reading the field strength" at each test frequency to create a test field meeting the need of standard, this result in long calibration time. In order to reduce the calibration time, the author deduced the relation between the signal output level and the field strength at reference point based on antenna theory, and made some experiments to verify the deduced relation. The experiments proved the correctness of the deduced relation. The author brought forward the "calculation approach method" for calibration and developed the RF-EMS automatic test software based on the deduced relation between the signal output level and the field strength at reference point. The practice indicated that the "calculation approach method" can accelerate the calibration process, shorten the calibration time and improve test efficiency.

articleTitle: A new FDTD parallel algorithm for wave propagation and absorption on big urban areas
abstract: Using FDTD to study wave propagation in big urban areas requires a huge amount of memory and processing time. This research deals with the problem of memory using a special formulation of 2-D FDTD to save memory. A system of linear equations is presented as a mathematical equivalent of Yee's equations. A recursive algorithm using Gaussian back-substitution is presented. It was adapted to parallel processing in a network of workstations and used to solve this system. Results that validate this approach are presented and the advantages and future improvements to this method are discussed.

articleTitle: Studies on crosstalk between microstrips
abstract: Crosstalk is a problem most PCB design engineers are interested in. On basis of transmission line theory, a simple analysis method of crosstalk between microstrips is proposed in this paper. With this method, common crosstalk can be predicted, so that proper design program is determined.

articleTitle: Characteristics of high frequency telecommunication cable
abstract: Differential copper serial links for high-speed data communication shorter than 20 meters are still a cost effective solution within a telecom system. Many of the transmission characteristics have to be taken into consideration when transmitting data with Gbit/s data rate. Several issues are discussed about the measuring methods and modelling techniques both for SI and EMI issues.

articleTitle: Radiation safety and environmental effects around cellular base stations of third generation DAMPS, DCS-1800, UMTS
abstract: An environmental survey for base stations of third generation DAMPS, DCS-1800, and UMTS cellular technology was performed for the largest cellular communications company in Israel - Cellcom Israel. The survey details potential environmental effects for man, ordnance, medical, aviation and industrial electronics and radiation hazards for fuel and chemicals. This paper cover risk subjects that include human exposure, ordnance, fuel and electronics. Regarding safety ranges for human exposure, the survey indicates the following. For a quantity of 23 transmitters in the sector of a DAMPS base station, the safety range at the antenna altitude level is 7 meters. In combining all possible transmitters without channel expansion, including DAMPS, DCS-1800 and UMTS, the safety range at the antenna altitude level is 7-m. When the DAMPS channels are expanded from 16 to 23 channels and the DCS-1800 is expanded from 4 transmitters to 6 transmitters, the safety range in relation to all transmitters increases to 8.2 m.

articleTitle: Using spectrum to extract texture feature
abstract: Extracting texture features is a key step in texture analysis. Various methods for texture analysis have been proposed (see Salari, E., Pattern Recognition, vol.28, no.12, 1993; Chen, J.L., Proc. ICASSP, vol.3, 1992). An efficient description of texture features is necessary, and the computational load is an important aspect. Recently, the texture spectrum method (see Wang, L. et al., Pattern Recognition, vol.25, no.3, 1992) has been developed. Compared with other methods, the concept of texture spectrum is clear, and its computational load is comparatively low. We studied texture spectrum, used it to extract texture features and obtained a more efficient description of texture. The paper introduces the principle of this method and gives test results. The results show the reasonableness of the new approach.

articleTitle: EMD from negative corona discharge
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic (EM) wave radiated from negative corona discharge has been investigated through a series experiments in which the discharge occurs in a set of needle-plate electrode in a closed loop circuit. The polarization pattern and orientation diagram under some different frequency have been presented and the results verify the assumption that the EM wave radiated from negative corona discharge in a closed loop circuit contains two components: one is from the equivalent short dipole antenna and the other from the equivalent little circular loop antenna. Experiment results will be useful for estimating the electromagnetic disturbance (EMD) from corona discharge.

articleTitle: Controlling conducted EMI emission on a Buck-boost converter using gate controlled circuit
abstract: The suppression of conducted EMI emissions of a Buck-boost converter using a gate controlled circuit is presented. The results indicate that the conducted EMI could be suppressed by controlling the rise and fall time of the gate signal when using a MOSFET as a switching device. The simulated results of the Buck-boost converter at a 100 kHz switching frequency are compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: The penetrating of EMP fields into a metal shielding enclosure by a slot
abstract: The shielding effectiveness to different sized slots in a shielding enclosure is calculated using the FDTD method. It is demonstrated that the resonance of a shielding enclosure's cavities and slots greatly influences a screened room's shielding effectiveness. Fast time-varying EMP couples more easily in a shielding cavity with slots.

articleTitle: Characterization of a reverberation chamber by 3D finite element method
abstract: This paper presents a 3D finite element method to simulate the electric field distribution in a reverberation chamber. The chi-square distribution for the square of electric field is obtained. The technique is effective to check the chi-square distribution and uniformity of the defined working volume at different frequencies close to lowest useable frequency with only one-time discretization of the chamber and objects in the chamber.

articleTitle: The characteristics of conducted EMI emission on PWM inverters with various PWM patterns
abstract: In this paper, characteristics of conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) emissions of three phase voltage source PWM inverters are presented. The conducted EMI emission levels of PWM inverters on various patterns: SPWM, DPWM60/spl deg/ and THIPWM techniques are focused. The experimental results of common mode EMI noises from the inverters are analyzed at the different modulation index and at various frequencies conditions. The results show the phenomena of EMI noises from the PWM inverters affect to intra systems.

articleTitle: The effect of resonance phenomena on the characteristics of a chamber
abstract: This paper describes the study of the effect of resonance phenomena on the chamber's characteristics, which mainly refers to the normalized site attenuation (NSA). The NSA test results of a 12.6/spl times/7.8/spl times/6 m/sup 3/ chamber are presented as an example to discuss the influence of resonance phenomena on the NSA characteristic of the chamber. A new structure of a chamber is put forward to eliminate the influence of the resonance phenomena and improve the NSA characteristic of the chamber.

articleTitle: ULF emission induced by tension and shear cracks
abstract: Penetration of low-frequency waves through a conductive medium due to the inductive seismo-electromagnetic effect is considered by a double-potential method. The source of electromagnetic waves induced by the movement of a conductive medium in a geomagnetic field is produced by tension and shear cracks. The analytical solution for tension cracks is obtained. The system of equations describing this process in the case of shear cracks in spherical coordinates is reduced to a two dimensional nonstationary system, which is solved by a second order algorithm that conserves some integral properties of the initial equations. Results are discussed.

articleTitle: Video display terminal EMI and human visual response
abstract: From a practical perspective, Electromagnetic Interference can indirectly impact work performance of the users of computer Video Display Terminals (VDT). Random variations in screen text or graphic images are typical results of EMI. The human visual system exhibits a physiological response to the display distortion. This paper examines effects of EMI on display terminals with actual case studies, and the human visual response known as Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS).

articleTitle: The top sound channel and formation low-frequency acoustic perturbations of top atmosphere
abstract: The conditions of the formation of acoustic wave packages formed in the top atmosphere by powerful pulse sources are considered. As sources directly influencing on the top atmosphere, the paper considers the flight of a rocket with a working engine at heights more than 100 km and strong earthquakes.

articleTitle: Control methods of EMI for modern radar
abstract: According to the characteristics of modem radar, this paper discusses the interference source and the propagation path of EMI. Several effective resisting interference measure are given about filtering, shielding and earth connection. The result proves that it improves the reliability of radar system.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of conducted electromagnetic emissions prediction in AC generator rectifier systems
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for modeling and simulation of conducted EMI prediction for widely used AC generator-rectifier systems. The mechanism of conducted EMI associated with a typical generator-rectifier system is analyzed. A high-frequency model of the generator is established. The system is simplified by a resonant circuit including the dominant stray distributed parameters. The conducted EMI of an actual system is investigated using time domain simulation. The validity of the models is confirmed by comparison to the laboratory measurements.

articleTitle: Signal integrity simulation and analysis in high-speed interconnects by using FDTD
abstract: With the advancements in microelectronics, interest in electromagnetic interference and compatibility in high-speed circuits has greatly increased in the engineering community, and applications of computational electromagnetics to electromagnetic interference and compatibility (EMI/EMC) engineering become an emerging technology. Termination, via, and crosstalk on interconnection lines will raise EMI problems in high-speed circuits and will therefore require more attention during the design phase for signal integrity. This paper presents signal propagation effect analysis on high-speed interconnection lines, between different parts, with the finite-difference time-domain method. The mechanisms and effectiveness of control measures are examined, which could be applied to high-speed circuit design.

articleTitle: Assessment of EMF radiation from a Ku-band antenna
abstract: This paper analyzes non-ionizing radiation levels of a uniformly illuminated horn antenna for land mobile earth station (LMES) application. Power flux density generated from the antenna at far field, near field, transition region, and equipment surface are calculated and assessed based on the method recommended by FCC. The analysis shows that the exposure levels satisfy the limits of International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) Guidelines, Council Recommendation 1999/519/EC of EU, CFR 47 FCC regulation and China EMF standard draft for both occupational exposure and public exposure.

articleTitle: A study on beam pattern forming for 8-element adaptive array in TDMA/TDD cellular communications
abstract: In this paper, an 8-element adaptive array, which based on a nonlinear decision feedback equalizer and recursive least squares algorithm is introduced for the post 3rd generation TDMA/TDD mobile communications. The formation of the beam pattern boosts up the desired directions and cancels the interference directions. Then the relationship between training sequence and beam pattern convergence is analyzed. Computer simulation results show the affiliation of beam forming and the directions of arrivals. The best length of training sequence for beam convergence is found.

articleTitle: Extrapolation of radiated-emission test data from 3 meters to 10 meters
abstract: It is a concern of many EMC students how to extrapolate radiated-emission test data from 3 m SAC to 10 m SAC. According to various heights of the radiator and different polarization patterns of the electrical waves, this paper presents a discussion of the above problem in the 30-1000 MHz frequency range. Accurate results have been obtained, which are valuable to practical measurements.

articleTitle: New approach for reflection and absorption of one-dimensional inhomogeneous anisotropic medium
abstract: A new numerical technique for reflection and absorption of a one-dimensional (1D) inhomogeneous anisotropic medium is presented. The waves propagating in the 1D anisotropic medium, as well as the incident plane wave with linearly polarized field, can be expressed as the sum of the right-circularly polarized (RCP) plane wave and the left-circular polarized (LCP) plane wave. After introducing the equivalent isotropic media for RCP and LCP plane waves, respectively, the scattering matrix method (SMM) for 1D nonuniform isotropic medium can be developed to deal with the anisotropic problem. Numerical results are shown and compared with the literature.

articleTitle: Research of information attributes of the VLF-range radiochannels for of the earthquakes forecast
abstract: In work based on the measuring-receiving complex, a comparative analysis of continuous records for the variation of amplitude of VLF-signals for the 3-rd radio stations results. As a result of observation of VLF-amplitude and their processing 3 possible recurrences of an image of the signal-harbinger were allocated which are observed on the average from 3 minutes to 28 hours before an earthquake. The time of display of the harbingers for earthquakes is more than 20 hours, and the distance between the VLF-link and the epicenter of the forthcoming earthquake is up to 2000 km. For earthquakes with depth more than 150 km the time of detection of the signal of a harbinger less than 12 hours and on distance from the VLF-link more than 4000 km.

articleTitle: The future trend of EMC in Taiwan
abstract: The Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI) has regulated EMC since 1997. It can be said that most manufacturers are familiar with EMC requirements and regulations since it has been implemented for many years. In order to have this process more understood, the author introduces a current BSMI equipment authorization program, including technical document reviews, and possible future actions. This paper discusses a new BSMI proposal, that will consider deregulating the equipment authorization process for peripheral equipment of personal computers, that is perhaps a first step towards an equipment approval process that will be consistent with these international developments.

articleTitle: Susceptibility analysis of electronic devices in ground vehicles to electromagnetic field radiated by cellular phones
abstract: We have conducted a theoretical study to compute the electromagnetic field level inside a typical ground vehicle due to a cellular phone. In this regard, the vehicle is first modeled by an appropriate 3-dimensional wire-grid structure while the cellular phone is approximated by a dipole antenna inside the vehicle. The governing Maxwell equations are then solved using an electric field integral equation method. Simulation results are presented to examine the electromagnetic field levels inside the vehicle due to the radiating dipole antenna with various polarizations. It is shown that the cellular phone acts to excite a resonant cavity representing the metallic compartment of the vehicle.

articleTitle: Microstrip line coupled triangular slot antenna
abstract: This paper describes the triangular slot antenna in the ground plane of the microstrip line. The slot antenna coupled by microstrip line is proposed, and the input impedance, S parameter and far field radiation patterns are obtained using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method.

articleTitle: Finite difference time domain simulation for multi-layer microwave absorber with frequency selective surface
abstract: A novel structure for broadband microwave absorption is introduced. It consists of multi-layer lossy materials with frequency selective surface on the interfaces and is backed by a metallic ground plane. Simulation and discussion are made, based on RCS reduction for finite size of the structure by using FDTD calculation.

articleTitle: Radio wave absorption analysis of coated elliptic cylinders with lossy magnetic ferrite films using conformal mapping method
abstract: Coated conductor elliptic cylinders with lossy absorption magnetic films which are useful components for electromagnetic compatibility are studied for electromagnetic wave reflection and scatterings. The conformal mapping method with integral equation using Green's function for lossy coated elliptic cylinders is applied to analyze the scattering characteristics of a mapped circular cylinder with lossy coated films.

articleTitle: A new method solving problems of electromagnetic shielding for a thin cylindrical shell of arbitrary cross section
abstract: A new method of solution for the electromagnetic shielding problems of a thin cylindrical shell of arbitrary cross section is presented. On the basis of averaged boundary conditions, we use the theorem of discontinuity of the normal derivative of a single-layer potential, integral equations of electromagnetic shielding for the thin cylindrical shell of arbitrary cross section are derived, and they are solved by using the method of boundary element. Compared with the solution obtained by using precise boundary conditions, the method presented is very simple and convenient. A foundation is laid for simple calculation of the electromagnetic fields from two sides out of the thin cylindrical shell and its shielding effectiveness.

articleTitle: On the electromagnetic characteristics of metallic-sprayed shells
abstract: The electromagnetic (EM) emission over 30 MHz /spl sim/1000 MHz is studied on the electronic pricing scale with and without metallic-sprayed cases. Results show that the metallic-sprayed cases can reduce the EM emission 22.5 dB /spl mu/m/m at the very most, average reduction is 16.1 dB /spl mu/m/m from an electronic pricing scale. The EM radiation attenuation models are developed based on the experiments. The errors of the attenuation models to the experiments are less than 5 dB /spl mu/m/m, the relative errors is less than 10%.

articleTitle: Study of lightning EMI on electronic equipment inside the microwave communication building
abstract: The strong electromagnetic field, which accompanies lightning stroking microwave tower or lightning cloud-to-earth discharging, can disturb the communication electronic equipment in microwave stations. This paper uses analytical calculation and numerical calculation to study this electromagnetic disturbance. Analytical calculation adopts an equation of cloud-to-earth discharging transient electromagnetic field. Numerical calculation uses difference method to calculate. The computed results of these two kinds of calculations both express that the magnitude of electromagnetic disturbance is decided by some correlation parameters, which are the magnitude of lightning electric current, /spl nu/ the travel speed of lightning electric current, h the height of the lightning current channel, d the calculated distance between the lightning current channel and the point of observation, etc. But numerical calculation can resolve the problem of medium mutation in microwave station building that makes it difficult to use analytical calculation to solve.

articleTitle: Preparation of modified textile possessed of absorbing and shielding characterizations
abstract: The electromagnetic wave theory of Schelkunoff has been studied. The condition of energetics and the reaction mechanism on depositing Ni-P alloy are investigated. Moreover, the modified textile possessed of the duplex characterization of absorbing and shielding effectiveness property is prepared by electroless coating. By analyzing three kinds of modified textile on both respects of microscopy and characterizations testing, the preparation conditions of the multifunctional and modified textile are put forward. The mol ratio of Ni/sup 2+/ to H/sub 2/PO/sub 2//sup -/ in the electroless Ni-P alloy coating solution directly influences the phosphorous proportion in the modified layer of textile. There are three frequency bands are studied in this paper: 30 MHz/spl sim/1000 MHz for SE, 12 GHz/spl sim/18 GHz and 100 kHz/spl sim/1.5 GHz for AE. The maximum of corresponding results are -80 dB (SE) at 265 MHz, -24.67 dB (AE) at 15.2 GHz and -12.28 dB (AE) at 435.1 MHz respectively.

articleTitle: Fast extraction of frequency dependent parameters of multiconductor transmission lines using hybrid method based Coifman wavelets
abstract: In this paper, we present a hybrid technique for calculation of frequency-dependent resistance and inductance with method of moments based on Coifman wavelets. The hybrid method combines a cross-section coupled circuit method with a surface integral equation approach. A coupled integral equation is then derived to relate these quantities through the diffusion equation inside the conductors and Laplace's equation outside. The method of moments is used to solve the integral equation. Instead of normal pulse basis, we use Coifman wavelets as expansion and testing functions. By using the one point quadrature technique, the computational time can be reduced greatly while maintaining the accuracy of same level.

articleTitle: Global regulatory requirements on CDMA mobile stations
