abstract: This paper addresses essential regulatory requirements, i.e., electromagnetic compatibility, radio spectrum, RF safety and electrical safety, for CDMA mobile stations. Technical standards in accordance with the essential requirements in USA, Europe and China are discussed and compared with each other.

articleTitle: Analysis for shielding effect of metal plate with apertures with FDTD
abstract: Aperture arrays for airflow in an enclosure can become the coupling path of electromagnetic interference (EMI) from the interior to the external environment. The FDTD (finite-difference time-domain) is a versatile computation technique for simulation of electromagnetic radiation in EMC analysis. Herein, the FDTD is applied to investigate the shielding effect (SE) of a metal plate with aperture arrays. The factors such as the size and shape of aperture, sum of apertures, the thickness of the metal plate are studied to see how they act on the SE. The numerical results and the measurement agree well. Some of the empirical conclusion will benefit the practical design.

articleTitle: Developing the universal RF-EMS automatic test software
abstract: This paper introduces the RF-EMS automatic test software developed by the author. In order to expend the scope of application, the RF-EMS automatic test software is designed to be compatible with many kinds of instruments used in the RF-EMS test made by different companies. In view of the general purpose, the paper explains the design thought and realization method. In addition, the feature of the software is described in detail.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic interference in low voltage secondary system of substation caused by short circuit fault
abstract: The electromagnetic interferences in low voltage secondary cable caused by short circuit fault were analyzed from two main routines coupling through CT and generating through grounding system, which would destroy control system and lead the main power apparatus damage. The calculated results were discussed.

articleTitle: Study of metallic modification on the surface of synthetic fibre with high shielding effectiveness
abstract: From the point of view of the theories of electromagnetic wave transmission, electrochemistry and modification, a metallic modification technique possessed of not only low cost but also endowing flexible materials composed of synthetic fibre with high shielding effectiveness is put forward. Morphologies and element analysis of the modified samples, which are coated with copper film or copper and nickel-iron duplex film, are carried out by SEM and EDX The shielding effectiveness of the samples is tested within the incident electromagnetic wave frequency range of 0.1 MHz/spl sim/1000 MHz and 1.5 GHz/spl sim/18 GHz. Two kinds of nickel-plating methods are compared. The SE of the best sample is between -93 dB and -110 dB within the frequency range from 0.1 MHz to 1000 MHz. The value is up to the first grade of shielding. The SE value of the modified samples reduces while the incident frequency rises from 1.5 GHz to 18 GHz. The SE value of the sample with nickel-iron outer layer is better than that of the sample with single nickel outer layer.

articleTitle: Research on EMC of inverter welder and welding arc
abstract: Inverter welders are one of the most useful electric welders in industry. An inverter welder is a complex and powerful load and its electromagnetic radiation should be noted. So it is essential to study the EMC of inverter welders and their welding arc. Here the mechanism of radiation from an inverter welder and its welding arc is analyzed, the calculation of the radiation is discussed, and some conclusions including the irradiation of welding workers are presented.

articleTitle: Modulation effect analysis by rotating screw metal fans
abstract: In this paper, the backscatter field of rotating screw metal fans is investigated based on PO/PTD (physical optics/physical theory of diffraction) and the method of equivalent currents (MEC), in conjunction with the quasi-stationary method. The time and frequency domain responses of the radar return signals are predicted. The modulation effects by the radar return signal of rotating screw metal fans are analysed. These results can be used in target identification.

articleTitle: Development of standard set for HF electrical field
abstract: This paper describes the standard set for the HF electrical field, which was completed using the "standard electrical field method". The standard transmitting antenna consists of thirteen half-wave tuned dipole antennas, whose operating frequencies are different. The frequency range covers from 30 to 1000MHz. The transmitting field strength is 100-120 dB/spl mu/V/m on the steel open area test site with dimensions of 40 m /spl times/ 1.5 m. Uncertainty is less than 1dB. It was used for EMC test such as the metrology of electromagnetic field strength and the calibration of antenna factor.

articleTitle: The radiated emission from discontinuities of PCB's traces
abstract: In this paper, the radiated emission from discontinuities (bend, T-junction and step) of PCB's traces are computed using the moment method. The input source is typical TTL clock signal. Results show that the radiation may be higher than the standard of EMC. So the radiated field from discontinuities of PCB's traces must be noticed.

articleTitle: Theoretical expressions for predicting shielding effectiveness of thin conducting films for the plane shield case
abstract: Thin conducting films or metallic films can be used to improve the performance of the plastic enclosures widely used by modern industry to produce economic container designs for electrical equipment. The transmission coefficients of thin metallic films in both the frequency and time domains are developed. The features of the two transmission coefficients in the time domain are pointed out. In addition, the transmission coefficient in the frequency domain can be directly used to predict shielding effectiveness, whereas the convolution of the arbitrarily incident waveform and the transmission coefficient in the time domain is introduced to analyze the property of the decay of the transmitted field.

articleTitle: Imaging of leakages from elliptical microwave applicator
abstract: A new study in the field of microwave imaging techniques is presented. Leakages from an elliptical microwave applicator is the corner-stone of the study. The diffracted fields due to the treated material and elliptical aperture are processed to obtain an image of the applicator end terminal. Subsequently, an exact determination of the maximum leakage values is carried out. The results are displayed in the form of three dimensional surfaces representing the changes of the leakage field intensity as a function of the aperture geometry,. Working frequency is 2.45 GHz and the principles can be applied to any microwave frequency.

articleTitle: The switching transient electric field measurements in a 500 kV substation
abstract: The transient electric fields generated by switching operations in the electric power substation were measured. These such measurements are the first one in China in the field of a high voltage substation. In either disconnect switches or circuit breakers being operated, a short line or a section of bus was energized or de-energized. The operations include closing or opening disconnect switches and circuit breakers. In this measurement many data was obtained and some characteristics of transient electric fields was presented in this paper. These conclusions concerning EMI level of switching transient electric fields are useful to engineering and theory analysis.

articleTitle: Measurement and examination of the relation between ionospheric scintillation expression methods in equatorial region
abstract: This paper examines a method for converting among scintillation expression methods, peak to peak values method and standard deviation values method, by using local measurement of meteorological parameters. Part 1 focuses on tropospheric scintillation related to 12.260 GHz measurements at an elevation angle of 59.9/spl deg/. Part 2 focuses on ionospheric scintillation at 3.916 GHz; observations were made at KMITL, Bangkok, Thailand. The principle techniques find a good correlation coefficient ranging from 0.900 to 0.999. As a result the relationship between two methods is given by /spl sigma//sub x/=/spl alpha/(p-p)+/spl beta/, where /spl alpha/ is 0.14.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic environment: Ap index and radioelectric power in VLF/LF
abstract: The object of this article is to establish if solar emissions can have consequences on the levels of power measured in places of weak latitudes compared to the equipment working out the solar index of activity. For that, we jointly use the results collected by the CTSN network and the solar indices of radiation Ap. The purpose of the network is to better understand the noise in the VLF/LF range. The equipment of acquisition is intended to record the amplitude of the vertical electric field (Ev) from 10 kHz to 80 kHz. They have collected this type of data for several years.

articleTitle: An accurate field matching analysis of ferrite phase shifter using ridged/grooved waveguide
abstract: In this paper we present an extension of the method based on the mode matching technique to analyze the ferrite phase shifter using ridged/grooved waveguide which has not been rigorously analyzed. Experimental tests have been carried out in order to verify the method. With higher modes considered, this method is superior to those in literatures published before.

articleTitle: Lightning electromagnetic environment assessment of software park near transmission lines
abstract: The lightning electromagnetic environments of planned Zhongguancun Software Park near transmission lines, including electrical field, magnetic field and grounding potential rise, are assessed by numerical analysis. From this analysis, we can conclude that the lightning strike is a serious threaten to the software park, protective countermeasures should be adopted to improve the electromagnetic environments of the software park.

articleTitle: EMC application in printed circuit boards with the attached cables
abstract: At high speeds, logic signals often appear jagged, and distorted because of ringing, reflection, crosstalk, radiation and EMI problems. Assuring the signal integrity is one basic problem faced by the PCB designers. This paper presents some general resolutions using the EMC theories, and shows how these theories are applied in a practical application in high-speed PCB designs.

articleTitle: Crosstalk effects from a cascaded line with different heights to a transmission line
abstract: Crosstalk or coupling characteristics between a cascaded line with an abrupt step on the way and a straight transmission line of finite length are discussed comparing measured and calculated results. To analyze the coupling phenomenon, a modified telegrapher's equation including the effects of external fields to the lines system is derived. The fields can be obtained by estimating vector potentials of currents in the line and the terminal sections, where the terminals are fabricated like a "via" configuration. A four-port network expression of the voltage and current at each terminal is obtained from solutions of the equation. We have done some experiments to appraise the utility of the theory used here by comparing the transmission characteristics.

articleTitle: A novel technique for indoor radio propagation modeling
abstract: Propagation prediction is important for designing indoor wireless communication systems. A technique combining ray tracing and the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is propounded to for modeling indoor radio propagation, in which ML (perfectly matched layer) absorbing boundary conditions are applied to FDTD meshes. The technique is described by considering a simple 2D environment.

articleTitle: Transient study of slots or apertures in PC main frame applying FDTD
abstract: The paper presents electromagnetic coupling of transient plane wave penetrating through slots or apertures perforated in one side of a shielded PC main frame. Several slots, simulating softdisc, CD-ROM, zip-disc and air vent, have been developed in one or more sides of the main frame. FDTD numerical method is applied to the studied model. Time-domain outputs are converted to frequency-domain responses using a FFT program for easy visualisation. Both time-domain and frequency-domain results are presented and discussed. The achieved results will be applicable to practical shielding enclosure design and electromagnetic interference protection.

articleTitle: The effect of slotted ground on digital signal
abstract: In this paper, we studied digital signal traveling along the trace over slotted ground. We used FDTD method to simulate electromagnetic distributing. Firstly, we analyzed the variety of digital signal in transmission process. At last, we obtained the relationship of the variety of signal with slot width, signal rise-time and the period of signal. We also analyse the mechanism responsible for the variety. Simulation result in this paper is very useful for the PCB design and other relevant works.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation for medium access control of WCDMA systems
abstract: For the increasing requirement of multimedia services in wireless networks, the dynamic reservation slotted multi-code medium access control protocol (MAC) is considered. The MAC is a kind of slotted, frame-based protocol with dynamic reservation and multi-code transmissions in a slot. An OPNET-based discrete event modeling and simulation method is developed to assess the uplink performance of the throughput in a cell. Better system performance can be achieved with dynamic reservation multi-code, according to the offered traffic load.

articleTitle: Distributed capacitance and inductance of transmission lines by considering the effects from ends and bends
abstract: A transmission line of finite length conductor with bend is considered. Explicit expressions for the per-unit-length parameters of the line are derived by using non-uniform transmission line approach and are verified by the method of moment.

articleTitle: Measurement of the transient fields from contact discharge
abstract: The transient electric fields caused by contact discharge in the IEC61000-4-2 standard set-up are measured using a broadband loaded V-antenna. The results show that: the spectrum of the radiated fields are not influenced by discharge voltage and polarity, but the longer distance away the discharge point is, the shorter bandwidth of spectrum is. The electric fields are different from the grounding point and the discharge point when discharging to horizontal coupling plane (HCP).

articleTitle: The general process to evaluate uncertainty in EMC measurement
abstract: A practical process, which is used to evaluate uncertainty in EMC measurement and is easy to popularize, according to the principle of uncertainty and conditions in EMC measurement, is presented. The issue of how to treat the sensitivity coefficient of some variables, whose relation with the measurement result is not very clear, is also discussed.

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis of electromagnetic field distribution around a small-size EMP simulator
abstract: A time-domain approach is presented to calculate electromagnetic fields around a small-size EMP simulator. The method employs the method of moments for numerical treatment of the governing electric field integral equation. Having obtained the field distribution around the developed EMP simulator, one can quantify the shielding requirements for nearby sensitive equipment.

articleTitle: A review of power control in cellular mobile communication systems
abstract: Current developments in power control research in cellular mobile systems are described. Typical algorithms including centralized PCA and distributed PCA are illustrated and analyzed. At the same time, the algorithms for multi-rate or multimedia wireless systems are discussed. The impact on the system performance of power control is then analyzed. Further work on power control algorithms for third generation cellular mobile system are presented.

articleTitle: A method for measuring Earth conductivity in non-uniform stratum
abstract: Based on the concept of apparent Earth conductivity (/spl sigma//sub k/), this paper provides a point of view that /spl sigma//sub k/ depends on the /spl rho//sub k/ value measured from only a power-supply polar distance (AB) by the four-electrode method, then an AB polar distance template for measuring /spl sigma//sub k/ in the non-uniform stratum is developed. The test results prove that the new method is feasible in the aspect of technology, and it has the significance of obviously improving work efficiency and working quality.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of EMI at main control room in Uljin nuclear power plant
abstract: In this paper, conducted and radiated noise at the power and enclosure ports of the plant control system and the core protection calculator installed at main control room in Uljin nuclear power plant were measured and analyzed. The measurement was performed continuously over a period of two months in which the power output was elevated progressively in phases from reactor power of 0% to 100%. The measurement consisted of performing conducted emissions in the frequency range of 30 Hz to 30 MHz, and radiated emissions in the frequency range of 30 Hz to 7 GHz. The measured values and profiles for conducted and radiated emissions were similar to those of nuclear plants gathered in United States. The conducted and radiated limits, which are applicable to Korean standard, using the recursive least square analysis technique were derived from measured data. The limits obtained were compared with those of United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission (USNRC) and Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI).

articleTitle: Measurement of terminal antennas in reverberation chamber
abstract: This paper proposes a method to measure the radiation efficiency of the terminal antenna in reverberation chamber. In this way, we can avoid the flaws of conventional methods and get a relatively accurate result. Finally, we point out the shortcomings of this method and some proposed ways to rectify it.

articleTitle: Dyadic Green's function for an unbounded gyroelectric chiral medium in cylindrical coordinate
abstract: Dyadic Green's function for an unbounded gyroelectric chiral medium is formulated in the Fourier domain in cylindrical coordinates. After a triple Fourier integral of the dyadic Green's function is obtained, a double one is reduced by performing integration over the longitudinal Fourier variable.

articleTitle: Seismo electromagnetics (latest results of NASDA's earthquake remote sensing frontier project)
abstract: NASDA (National Space Development Agency of Japan) has been conducting the Earthquake Remote Sensing Frontier Project since 1996 within the framework of the Earthquake Frontier Projects (for which the author is the principal scientist) by S.T.A. (Science and Technology Agency). The main emphasis of NASDA's Frontier Project is the complete understanding of lithosphere-atmosphere-ionosphere (LAI) coupling by means of different kinds of observational items and finally we would like to contribute to short-term earthquake prediction. We show our latest results on different subjects (subionospheric VLF/LF propagation, ULF emission etc.).

articleTitle: A novel EMC prediction method for power electronic converter
abstract: A novel EMC prediction method of power converter is presented, which combines the simple test means with appropriate system recognition method, obtains the EMI nonparametric model by test, and obtains the EMI parameter model by the system recognition method to predict EMC of a power converter. The method has been verified in a power inverter.

articleTitle: Analysis on propagation of the electromagnetic waves associated with earthquakes
abstract: According to the radial theory and waveguide theory, the paper deals with several problems about propagation of the electromagnetic waves associated with earthquakes. It is supposed that ULF and VLF SEMSs which could propagate far are mainly via groundwaves. The cut-off frequency for the atmosphere-crust wave guide is also estimated.

articleTitle: Leakage current variations of power drive systems with EMI input filters
abstract: The definition of leakage currents for electrical equipment with regard to safety aspects is commonly known and included in most relevant safety standards today. However, this leakage current is usually measured at the typical 50 or 60 Hz frequency of the power supply network.

articleTitle: A practical approach to measure the hybrid absorber characteristics
abstract: This paper describes a practical approach to measure the characteristics of a hybrid absorber, which is represented by its reflecting coefficient. A log periodic antenna and illuminative wall are used in the measurement and this approach is very simple and practical. The accuracy of this approach increased with the directional characteristics of the antenna. Also, the calculation of the reflecting coefficient of the hybrid absorber is made by using the FDTD numerical method. There is good agreement between the measurement results and the calculation results.

articleTitle: The solution of harmonic restriction for motor speed regulation
abstract: An EMC standard for higher request of restriction on harmonic currents is administrated compulsively since 2001. The harmonic current generated by motor speed regulation is harmful to the power system. It must be regulated within the limits according with new EMC standards. The traditional regulation method cannot pass these standards. The new solutions are found here after analyzing and simulating the performance of on-off modulation and high frequency modulation.

articleTitle: The introduction of Taiwan's product inspection and certification
abstract: At the beginning of 2002, Taiwan joined the World Trade Organization (WTO). Therefore, product inspection and certification needs to be the last procedure before products can be put in the marketplace. In this paper, the authors introduce how much and what kind of inspection and certification needs to be done for ITE product, electrical & electronics equipment and telecommunications equipment and discusses certified marks.

articleTitle: The analysis of interference immunity of the LAN
abstract: The transmission media in common use of the LAN-twisted pair may couple with an external electromagnetic field, the field can excite common-mode (CM) current and differential-mode (DM) current. To evaluate the differential-mode current, this paper proposes a comparatively stricter new method: the bifilar-helix-method based on the reciprocity theorem. To evaluate the common-mode current, the finite element method (FEM) is applied.

articleTitle: Analyzing and controlling on the radiation interference of DC/DC module
abstract: The EMI design of a DC/DC module is the key for the EMC designing of devices, and Common Mode (CM) noise is crucial for the EMI of DC/DC modules. The generating of CM noise is clarified and the control techniques are presented in this paper. The efficiency of the control techniques is verified by an instance with measurement data.

articleTitle: Design and optimization method for a type dielectric lens
abstract: A new type of dielectric lens used for the compact-field test is designed in this paper. The main formulation for such a design is based upon the geometrical optics method. The light path-differences are chosen as the objective function to implement the optimization. After the contour of the lit side of the lens is theoretically optimized, the mathematical function expression of the contour is obtained. The transmitted electromagnetic waves across the lens are proven to be approximately plane waves within /spl plusmn/20/spl deg/ scanning angle. Finally, the light path-differences between one which is with lens and one which is without lens are compared which demonstrates that the existence of such a lens is very effective for making the propagated wave much closer to a plane wave.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of impulse EMI waveform in HV lab
abstract: A new method is introduced to measure and analyze the EMI in high voltage laboratory. The measuring system includes a hardware system and a software analyzer. The accepted interference signal is analyzed in time domain, frequency domain and synchronously in joint time-frequency domain based on the wavelet theory. The results show clearly the component and amplitude of the interference signal in different frequency range and transmitted through different ways such as radiation or conduction.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic field of metal bar moving across geomagnetic field in a conducting half-space
abstract: The electromagnetic fields of a horizontal electric dipole and arbitrary current element on a metal bar are derived employing the Hertz vector method. According to this result, the expressions of the electromagnetic field generated by the metal bar moving across a geomagnetic field are obtained. This study is the theoretical basis of further research on the electromagnetic field of a ship moving across the Earth's magnetic field in water.

articleTitle: Measurement and evaluation of pulsating environmental magnetic fields by the example of resistance welding installations
abstract: Resulting from the connection between the change rate of a magnetic field and the induced currents in an exposed human body, pulsating magnetic fields have to be evaluated analyzing the waveforms of the field or the field-generating current. Considering the specific output current waveforms of resistance welding installations in the paper appropriate procedures to determine the waveform-dependent exposure limits are explained by the example of a resistance welding inverter. Based on investigations of the field distribution the actual flux density values are compared to the ascertained exposure limits.

articleTitle: Study of interference and damage experiments on electronic equipment in transient and stable EM field
abstract: Electronic equipment is interfered with or damaged from outside in many ways. In all cases the EM field imports some interference through the shelled devices' apertures, however the main interference is introduced through the connecting lines. Some electronic equipment can be interfered with by magnetic pulse without metallic shields. But in the past, people didn't pay enough attention to the influence, even the magnetic pulse by lightning or abrupt actions of the high voltage switch devices. These can cause the parameters to change, performance to decline or the equipment to misoperate, even the equipment to be damaged. The paper gives some experiments to analyze in order to make clear how much the interference can endure.

articleTitle: Use of low voltage power networks for data transmission. EMC issues and standardization problems
abstract: The use of the low voltage power network for data transmission can produce radiated disturbances. In order to determine field limits when using this technique and methods to check this limit, a procedure must be defined and a standard must be written. The paper presents the technique used to transmit information through the low voltage distribution network, the difficulties to define limits for the radiated field and a field measurement method to check this limit in case of conflict. The coupling factor is defined and experimental results of the measured coupling factor and of the longitudinal conduction loss are presented. The progress of the standardization work is also discussed.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of shielding effectiveness of metal-coating plastics for information terminals
abstract: Metal-coating plastics are being used as shielding materials for electronic and information terminals due to their light weight. In this paper, a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm was newly proposed for analyzing the shielding effectiveness of metal-coating plastics in a broad frequency band. The method was based on the derivation of a time-domain representation of the surface resistance of an equivalent resistive film. The validity of the proposed algorithm, for both far-field and near-field shielding, was verified by comparing the calculated results with theoretical ones. Good agreement was found between them when the size of the shielding material is sufficiently large compared to the wavelength.

articleTitle: Assessment of the risk of damage due to lightning in the information systems
abstract: During the assessment of the risk of damage due to lightning in the information systems, some main factors should be taken into account, such as surroundings and importance of the information systems. This paper discusses a method of assessment and the selection of surge protective devices (SPDs). An example is provide in this paper to show how the risk assessment can be applied for a telecommunication site with an adjacent antenna mast.

articleTitle: Study on space electromagnetic field shielding effectiveness of knife shielding door
abstract: Based on equivalent circuit theory, we obtain a range of variation of the key parameters which affect the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of a knife shielding door. A law of effectiveness change in the range is presented. Simulated data shows that shielding effectiveness of the door in some frequency range is fairly satisfactory.

articleTitle: Simulation on the electromagnetic radiation of PCB
abstract: The article gives the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of the A/D converter. The A/D converter is a double integrating type. The PCB layout of the A/D converter is formed with the software layout plus in OrCAD. Two PCB arrangement prototypes of the A/D converter are studied. For each kind of device arrangement, the electromagnetic radiation characteristics are studied using special software Omega Plus for 4- or 2- layer PCB.

articleTitle: A model of M distribution for the propagation of electromagnetic wave from the micro power
abstract: M distribution is a potential model for the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves. This theoretical distribution was fitted for the data collected in several short-distance environments in Beijing city, and the results prove that the M distribution model is suitable for the study of propagation characteristics of electromagnetic wave from the micro power.

articleTitle: A novel model of crosstalk in ultra-high-frequency microstrip transmission lines
abstract: In this paper, a novel model of crosstalk in ultra-high-frequency microstrip transmission lines is proposed. Analogous to dielectric relaxation considerations of Cole-Cole diagrams as applied to dielectric materials, a "reactive relaxation" concept is introduced to represent the frequency-dependent characteristics of coupled microstrip lines. Relevant algorithms are useful in computer-aided circuit designs.

articleTitle: Observations on the leader-return stroke of cloud-to-ground lightning with the broadband interferometer
abstract: Radio frequency observations of cloud-to-ground lightning (CG) were made the broadband lightning interferometer. Radiation source locations and electric field waveforms have been analyzed for different types of breakdown events, including the preliminary breakdown of in-cloud activities, the stepped leaders of initial strokes to ground and activities during and following return strokes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the potential distribution in a relay cell generated by a direct lightning strike in a 500 kV substation
abstract: The protection and controlling devices have been moved into the relay cell in the switchyard from the controlling building in some newly-built 500 kV substations in China. The transient grounding potential rise will be caused in a relay cell by a direct lightning strike in a 500 kV substation and be harmful to the secondary devices. Therefore, it is very important to predict the transient potential distribution in the relay cell. The authors calculated and analyzed the transient grounding potential distribution, found the appropriate mode of the inner grounding grid in the relay cell. Thus, the electromagnetic interference that the protection and controlling devices will suffer from the transient grounding potential rise in the relay cell can be reduced greatly.

articleTitle: Thevenin equivalent circuit-based time domain simulation for conducted EMI in lossy transmission lines
abstract: This paper presents a time domain simulation model for conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) in lossy transmission lines. The lossy lines are divided into a small number of ideal sections for which the Thevenin equivalent circuits substitute, and between these sections the resistances and conductances are connected on behalf of the loss of lines. The novel algorithm yields accurate results, is efficient without any numerical integration and suitable for transient simulation of conducted EMI in conductors, PCB tracks and cables.

articleTitle: The analysis and research of the radio propagation models in multifloored buildings
abstract: The paper reviews the models for predicting the indoor radio propagation, using classical models of radio propagation to analyze the merits and defects of the floor attenuation factors and the path loss exponent, when they are used in practical prediction. A specific building has been measured and compared at two different frequency bands, which gave relatively good results.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the influence of the surrounding buildings on the performance of a grounding grid
abstract: By the use of numerical method, the influence of the surrounding buildings on the performance of a real small testing grounding grid is researched. Experiments have been done to verify the numerical method. The performance of the grid considering the surrounding buildings is compared with that not considering the surrounding buildings. From the experiments and the calculation, it can be seen that the influence of the surrounding buildings is very small. Both the method and the results are useful for designing the grounding grids of the substations in city.

articleTitle: Full wave analysis of microstrip discontinuities
abstract: In this paper, we present a full-wave analysis of microstrip discontinuities, including open-end, gap and dummy line. First, the Green's function for dielectric slab is derived in a tensor form and the Sommerfeld integrals are carefully treated by pole extraction technique and folding approach. Then the integral equation formulated is solved by method of moments to obtain the current distribution along and transmission line and the S-parameters. With the scattering matrix given, the equivalent circuit parameters are also extracted. The phenomenon of resonance induced by dummy line is studied in the paper as well.

articleTitle: Crosstalk in fiber Raman amplification for multi-channel WDM system
abstract: The paper produces the SIR (signal-interference-ratio) formula for fiber Raman amplification in an N-channel system based on the coupled equation of SRS (stimulated Raman scattering). It analyses the SIR of fiber Raman amplification in a three-channel system and the relations between the SIR and the pump wave power and signal wave power. Another topic discussed is the relationship between the SIR and the number of channels. The conclusion is drawn that there is obvious crosstalk in multi-channel Raman amplification, even if it works in linear amplification. The limiting condition for applying fiber Raman amplification is presented.

articleTitle: Analyzing and controlling on the radiation interference of DC/DC module
abstract: EMI designing of the DC/DC module is a key for the EMC designing of devices, Common Mode (CM) noise is crucial for the EMI of DC/DC module. The generating of CM noise is clarified and the controlling techniques are presented in this article, the efficiency of the controlling techniques is verified by an instance with measurement data.

articleTitle: Frequency domain simulation of the EM internal noises in the matrix VLSI with orthogonal topology of power supply feeding
abstract: In this paper the problem of frequency domain simulation of the EM internal noises in the chip has been considered. The new 3-D mathematical model (MM) of the electromagnetic noise distribution in the chip with orthogonal topology of power supply feeding has been developed. On to the basis of the developed MM the software simulation of the EM noise distribution in the chip has been done.

articleTitle: Path loss prediction of electromagnetic wave from the micro power
abstract: Results of the measurement of electromagnetic waves from the micro power conducted in short-distance environments at 900 MHz and 1800 MHz are presented. The data were obtained in four different environments in Beijing. Some analytical models are presented to predict the path loss in short distance. These models show that the path loss exponent value is close to the value n=2 in a suburban open field environment which is for free-space propagation, and is n=3 or so in other three urban environments.

articleTitle: Analytical evaluation of the asymptotic impedance matrix of a uniaxial substrate with roof-top functions
abstract: An asymptotic technique is presented to solve the asymptotic part of the impedance matrix in the spectral domain for printed circuit structures on a uniaxial substrate by using roof-top subdomain expansions. The infinite double integral of the asymptotic part of the impedance matrix is reduced to a finite one-dimensional integral by performing the integral transform technique. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method are compared with those of the conventional method, and it is demonstrated that the proposed method reduce the computation and improve the accuracy for the anisotropic uniaxial case.

articleTitle: Study on ESD characteristics and its effect mechanism
abstract: Based on experimental study on microcircuit and electric explosive device (EED) applied by electrostatic discharge (ESD), the characteristics and its electric conduction law of ESD are introduced. And it is shown that the generally accepted Ohm's law is not followed at times under very high electrostatic field. In another words, ESD discharge curve is not an exponential decay one. ESD may form a hazard to microcircuit and EED. And its effect mechanism includes thermal effect of adiabatic process, electromagnetic interference from broadband electromagnetic radiation, overstress in high potential electrostatic field and field-caused breakdown effect etc. The failure rate may reach about 50% for unprotected MOS circuits and 10% for bipolar circuits due to general ESD hazards. The electrostatic ignition energy of EED is smaller with 2-3th power than that of the EED which is ignited through electrifying.

articleTitle: The performance of Bluetooth network with self interference
abstract: Bluetooth network performance in the presence of self interference is evaluated by simulation. Self interference arises because different piconets' frequency hopping and clocks are asynchronous. The performance criteria used are FER (frame error rate) and throughput. The relation between performance and piconet number is studied by simulation.

articleTitle: Automatic measurement system of the disturbance power of household electrical appliances and electric facilities
abstract: The automatic measurement system is designed to test the disturbance power of household electrical appliances and electric facilities. In this paper, the author introduces the whole set of the system, and describes the test software.

articleTitle: Large scale computing system EMC design challenges and solutions
abstract: With the ever increasing number of EMC compliance requirements that information technology equipment (ITE) must meet in order to satisfy world wide shipments, the job of an EMC engineer is getting more and more difficult. In this paper the challenges and solutions associated with designing large scale computing systems to meet the miscellaneous EMC requirements are given using the latest IBM S/390 Z900 CMOS mainframe system as an example.

articleTitle: The influence of manufacturing tolerances on the magnetic field of compensated three-phase power cables
abstract: Due to compensation effects the magnetic field of a twisted three-phase power cable built up by 3 wires of finite length can be reduced by splitting each conductor into N smaller wires. Maximum compensation occurs if the 3N conductors are placed on their exact positions prescribed by the theory. In reality the perfect order is affected by tolerances of the manufacturing process. Compared with the ideal 3N-wire cable this leads to higher field values. By our investigation we found that despite the impairing influence of inaccuracies the split of the 3-wire cable leads to a remarkable field reduction in the range from 30 to 50 dB. Attenuation diagrams show how the field of the 3N-wire cable depends on different splitting steps N and on the jitter domain /spl Delta//spl Phi/ of the random angle deviation of the wires.

articleTitle: A study on perturbation mode of microwave heating substrate temperature-field
abstract: The paper presents a new technique, i.e. by microwave design of microwave heating substrate (MHS), presents a microwave axial symmetry temperature field model and finds the general solution by using a perturbation method. On this basis, we design a so-called synthesis dielectric heating substrate and obtain the optimized and larger uniform temperature-field areas than the diameter of the substrate holder in a microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD) system.

articleTitle: The acquisition and processing of computer electromagnetic leakage and its realization research
abstract: The research on computer electromagnetic leakage draws more and more attention in the modern electromagnetic field. The study on testing and processing approaches of leakage signal is not only a subject considered by the Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC), but also the essential techniques for security (TEMPEST) and anti-steal of computer information. This paper presents frequency domain testing method and the research of its practical testing based on the GTEM device. It also provides the acquisition method of temporal signal and its analysis.

articleTitle: Simulation of lightning magnetic field
abstract: The lightning magnetic field is simulated when a pulse current is injected into the loop from the lightning surge generator. Different waveforms of lightning magnetic field can be simulated by regulating the parameters of the loop according to the relation between the parameters of the loop and the simulated wave. The dot loop is made to measure the magnetic field in the big loop and the results show that the M-field is relative even among a curtain area of the big loop, which is appropriate to test the lightning M-field effect on electromagnetic sensitive devices.

articleTitle: Selection of the anti-EMP primary filtering devices in the power network and calculation study
abstract: The main technology measures of anti-EMP in the civil defense shelter department's power network are limiting and filtering circuits. High voltage and low voltage zinc-oxide (ZnO) lightning arresters are commonly selected for limiters. Filtering includes primary filtering and precise filtering. In primary filtering devices, the low voltage non-power compensation condenser components are commonly changed into star connection and grounding. Before entering the high shielding area, special precise power filters, which are more expensive, are fitted. However, up to now, nobody has researched how to design and calculate the primary filtering devices in detail. We present methods for designing, selecting and calculating primary filtering devices, based on more than ten years' design experience. A table is presented of capacitor groups and capacitor value changes required for the design.

articleTitle: Predicting the general electromagnetic radiation level of high speed railway by the static parameters of pantographs and networks
abstract: In this paper, interrelation analysis between the electromagnetic radiation (ER) emitted by a electrified railway line and its static parameter of pantographs, and networks (SPPN) were carried out. It is concluded that there is close interrelation between them. According to the interrelation. the general level or the ER emitted by the high speed railway in China were predicted by its SPPN.

articleTitle: Several methods of radar data fusion
abstract: In the processing of radar data, target estimation states fusion is an important problem. Especially under the decentralized model, various estimations of target state which come from local filters with Kalman filter may be fused in order to obtain a more accurate target estimation state. There are two problems to be solved. The first is the fusion criterion, different fusion criteria bring out different results. Three fusion criteria are discussed; one is based on the covariance matrix of estimation error, the second is dependent on the infinite normal number, and the last is related to the element of the state vector. The second problem is the tracking algorithm; it affects the accuracy of the state fusion result. The three criteria and their corresponding algorithms are presented. The algorithms estimating target state are set up with a strong tracking filter other than Kalman or extended Kalman filter; they have better tracking performance so that they can overcome the deficiencies related to Kalman or extended Kalman filters. The reason for this is explained. Comparison results are given.

articleTitle: The development of third generation mobile telecommunication systems in China
abstract: The paper presents briefly the current situation of development of mobile communications in China. A comparison is made of the distinctions in the air interface of the physical layer between 3GPP and 3GPP2. It is necessary to further harmonize various standards to achieve a unique global 3G standard.

articleTitle: Innovative absorbing-boundary conditions for the efficient FDTD analysis of transient EMP interaction problems
abstract: The paper deals with a modified version of the Fang-Mei's super-absorption algorithm for the truncation of three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) meshes combined with an innovative low pass filtered algorithm to assure numerical stability of the FDTD procedure for late time. The proposed method is usually applied to analysis of slow-decaying transient problems, such as the lightning or nuclear electromagnetic pulse interaction with a cable or complex structures. Numerical results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: HEMP coupling to circuits inside the shielding box with a penetrative wire
abstract: HEMP coupling to circuits inside the shielding box with a penetrative wire is studied using the FDTD method. Results show that a penetrative wire can make the HEMP induced current in circuits inside the shielding box increase greatly through coupling with the incident field and the scattering field of the shielding box. This is useful for estimating the HEMP coupling to electronic apparatus and systems such as radios and computers.

articleTitle: EMI in hydropower plant and EMC design for its computer monitoring and control system
abstract: Computer monitoring and control system (CMCS) is important to upgrade the automation degree in hydropower plant. Aimed at raising the system ability against EMI problems, this paper first discusses EMI in hydropower plant. It presents specific interference sources and objects, for protection. It also remind the frequent problems occurred. Then the paper achieves a proper EMC design of CMCS on both general and partial considerations. They refer to power supply system, course and transmission channel and computer room mainly. Some specific applications of design based on basic EMC techniques are also given in the paper. They are, mainly about grounding, shielding etc. With the introduction of this paper, it is practical to realize the optimal effect against interference especially for CMCS in hydropower plant.

articleTitle: EMI suppression for frequency converter application
abstract: This paper analyzes the EMC problems and main EMI sources for the actual application of a frequency converter. It presents EMI suppression measures and proposals and introduces key frequency converter EMC techniques. It also provides examples and effects in actual engineering.

articleTitle: 20 Years of professional experience in international EMC-labs
abstract: Is EMC/telecom (CE) testing a business or just another regulatory requirement? Can EMC be a potential trade barrier between Asia and the EU? The following issues are considered. Tricks of the trade in global EMC compliance (CE, MRA, norms, clients). Consequences if manufacturers do not take EMC serious. EMC management (20Y) in small, medium and large EU corporations. Competition in EU (Germany) EMC markets. Why should your lab be ISO/EN 17025? Procedure, cost and benefits. Planning, investing, marketing, operating, staffing and managing labs. Calibration, measurement uncertainty (k = 2) traceability, employee training. First results of the 100 German EMC inter-lab-comparison test. German DAR auditor (10Y) experience in quality and technical assessment. Which common deficiencies in the labs do frequently occur? Illustrative case studies of auditing EU and Asian test labs. Can Asia avoid western world mistakes? This is all embedded in a critical review and analysis of politics, technology, interpretation of norms and lab service quality.
